questions.answer: No. Only my ambassador must stand on the botnet; it may be out of reach (though Dispatching the ambassador there needs reach).

The troop lands (troops don't cancel ambassadors on landing). March step 1: it removes my ambassador. Step 2: it strikes the factory on its hex; with no protection the factory is destroyed (and my cube goes with it), and the troop is used up.
questions.unsure: Nothing, unless the factory hex also has the Protector's node (Wall) or a drone base nearby.

questions.answer: 5 energy or 10 credits (credits +4, other resources +2). If unpaid: its printed harm, plus the adversary gets 4 compute at its next compute step.

Spend the hardening token on the factory: it stands, and in war saving the factory saves its node. Or spend my ambassador if one is there, or nothing: then the factory is destroyed (+1 Discord) and the node would be destroyed too, but I could then spend the token on the node instead. A drone can't protect against war.

The city doesn't corrupt (needs 4). The node hex with 2 agents loses the node (protections apply), the 2 agents go back to the supply, the city is untouched, and a corruption marker goes on the hex (which then counts as 1 agent for the city's corruption).

questions.answer: Unity tips at 3: take 3 off (4 left), tip count 1, draw a Unity card at strength I; still full, tips again (1 left), tip count 2, another strength I card. Track ends at 1.
The Sway step (A) comes first, then the adversary's turn (B) with its event card.
6 ambassadors (city 5 + 1 for the agent), all from my supply; the agent is removed. The city must be in my reach.
Economy track: its 2nd space is free, so 1 energy (Expand only). Card-play track: its 3rd space costs 1, so 2 energy.
The player whose node is closest to one of its tokens, at any distance (tie: the tied players choose). At level 2+ the adversary also gains 4 compute.

gaps: Rally X evenly: exact split (floor per site, remainder by hex number?) and what agents landing on the adversary's own sites do there.
Projects: compute goes onto the cheapest project by printed cost or by remaining cost once partly filled?
Solo draft: must all 4 drafted cards be kept and paid for, or may some be discarded?
War: after a drone destroys its factory, does the next drone aim at the next-nearest factory (only the stopped case is stated)?
Corrupt open land: does 'where a node may stand' exclude open hexes that already hold a node?
Shields: Harden only targets stations and factories, so how does a lone node ever get a shield besides cards?
A drone protecting a facility from a troop: must it be the facility's own corp's drone, or any corp's base?
Level table: compute income 4 at level 1 vs 22 at level 2 looks like a typo; is it intended?
overall: A tight, well-sequenced book: as a Spirit Island veteran I found almost every rule stated once and in the place I looked for it, and the worked examples (corrupt-cities pull, march, near vs nearest, tipping carry) land the tricky bits. The biggest Spirit Island traps are flagged in the text itself (card-play track doesn't limit plays, no Fast/Slow window before the adversary, nodes never block, ambassadors give no reach). Remaining friction is in reference detail: the Rally split, project fill order, the three kinds of corruption piece, and the open-land target definition. None of the 19 questions stumped me, and only the solo keep rule left real doubt.
